stories.title: CISA Adds 10 Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
stories.abstract: CISA has added multiple vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, most notably a critical command injection flaw in Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Router. Attackers are actively exploiting these weaknesses to execute arbitrary commands with root-level privileges.
stories.why: Active exploitation of root-level command injection vulnerabilities poses a severe risk of full system compromise and unauthorized network control.
stories.action: Update Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Router to versions 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3, or later.

stories.title: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
stories.abstract: Drupal has disclosed a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-136716, involving improper error handling that allows for unauthorized access. The flaw is currently being exploited in the wild, necessitating immediate attention for all Drupal core installations.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical access bypass vulnerabilities in core CMS frameworks poses an immediate risk of full site compromise and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update Drupal core to versions 10.6.23, 11.3.23, or 11.4.14 immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit 10 Vulnerabilities Across Mitel, Juniper, Vates, and Danfoss Products
stories.abstract: CISA has added ten security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including five critical vulnerabilities affecting Mitel MiCollab software. These additions confirm that attackers are actively leveraging these specific weaknesses in real-world campaigns.
stories.why: Active exploitation of enterprise communication software poses a significant risk for unauthorized access and potential lateral movement within corporate networks.
stories.action: Update Mitel MiCollab to a version beyond 10.3.0.18 immediately.

stories.title: PostgreSQL security advisory (AV26-1211)
stories.abstract: Multiple vendors have released security advisories covering critical vulnerabilities. Affected software includes PostgreSQL's psqlODBC driver, SolarWinds Dameware and Serv-U products, and Erlang/OTP. These flaws range from memory corruption and command injection to privilege escalation via path traversal.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure to remote code execution and unauthorized system access, with one flaw already appearing on the CISA KEV catalog.
stories.action: Update psqlODBC, SolarWinds Dameware, Serv-U, and Erlang/OTP to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
stories.abstract: 1Password reported a security breach involving its backend infrastructure. An unauthorized party gained access to specific customer data by compromising an employee's GitHub account. The company confirmed that encrypted password vaults and sensitive user secrets remained secure and were not accessed during the incident.
stories.why: Supply chain and third-party platform compromises remain a significant vector for accessing internal corporate systems and sensitive customer metadata.

stories.title: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension
stories.abstract: A new infostealer dubbed Remus is harvesting Gmail data by masquerading as a legitimate Google Sheets browser extension. Threat actors are promoting this capability as a zero-day exploit to compromise user email accounts through malicious Chrome add-ons.
stories.why: This highlights a persistent risk where browser extensions bypass standard security controls to exfiltrate sensitive cloud-based communications.
stories.action: Audit installed Chrome extensions and remove any unauthorized or suspicious browser add-ons.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | Hunting LANDFALL: From Overlooked Images to State-Linked Mobile Spyware
stories.abstract: Researchers identified LANDFALL, a sophisticated Android spyware framework that leverages zero-day vulnerabilities in Samsung's image processing library. Delivered via malformed DNG files, the malware enables zero-click compromises, with evidence suggesting its use in targeted surveillance campaigns across multiple regions.
stories.why: It highlights the ongoing risk of zero-click exploits targeting image parsers, which bypass traditional user interaction defenses to facilitate state-sponsored mobile surveillance.

stories.title: Microsoft: China’s Salt Typhoon hackers are using Artex
stories.abstract: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored threat actors from China and North Korea are adopting an offensive AI framework known as ARTEX. This tool automates reconnaissance and exploitation tasks, significantly accelerating the speed at which attackers can compromise vulnerable systems.
stories.why: The integration of agentic AI into state-sponsored toolkits lowers the barrier for complex attacks and drastically reduces the window for incident response.

stories.title: FIFA says hackers accessed ‘limited set of personal and business information’
stories.abstract: FIFA confirmed a recent cyberattack resulted in unauthorized access to internal business and personal data. The organization is currently collaborating with law enforcement to investigate the scope of the breach, though specific details regarding the timeline and affected information remain undisclosed.
stories.why: Large international organizations are frequent targets for data exfiltration, posing significant privacy risks to employees and business partners.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports of active exploitation. These include an SSRF flaw in N-able MailAssure and a zero-day vulnerability affecting the MONAI Label medical imaging framework.
stories.why: Active exploitation of these flaws in enterprise and specialized infrastructure poses a significant risk of unauthorized internal network access and data compromise.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label immediately.

stories.title: Hackers now exploit critical Drupal RCE flaw to hijack sites
stories.abstract: Drupal developers have confirmed active exploitation of a critical remote code execution vulnerability. Attackers are currently leveraging this flaw to gain unauthorized control over unpatched websites, prompting urgent warnings for administrators to secure their installations against ongoing compromise attempts.
stories.why: Remote code execution flaws in content management systems provide attackers with full administrative control, facilitating data theft and persistent backend access.
stories.action: Update Drupal to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Agency Takes Some Systems Offline After Cyber Intrusion
stories.abstract: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, a branch of the U.S. Treasury, has suspended certain systems following a security breach. The agency is currently investigating unauthorized access to a restricted portion of its infrastructure and has extended reporting deadlines for financial institutions.
stories.why: The compromise of a federal agency handling sensitive financial intelligence and suspicious activity reports poses significant risks to national and economic security.

stories.title: Two Newly Disclosed GeoServer Vulnerabilities Under Attack
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning for two high-severity vulnerabilities within GeoServer. These flaws allow for unauthenticated remote code execution when combined with other existing security weaknesses in the platform.
stories.why: Unauthenticated remote code execution poses a critical risk to infrastructure integrity and data confidentiality for organizations hosting geospatial data services.
stories.action: Update GeoServer to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect, identified as CVE-2026-84869. The flaw allows unauthorized guests to execute malicious payloads on the host machines of MSP technicians, potentially granting full control over the targeted systems.
stories.why: MSP environments are high-value targets; compromising a technician's workstation provides attackers with broad, privileged access to the networks of multiple downstream clients.
stories.action: Update ConnectWise ScreenConnect to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ASP.NET Anti-CSRF Library Flaw Allowing Unauthenticated RCE
stories.abstract: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-131914, has been identified in the legacy Idunno.AntiCsrf library for ASP.NET. Attackers are actively exploiting this flaw, which carries a CVSS score of 9.3, to compromise unpatched systems.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code, posing a severe risk to any application still utilizing this deprecated library.
stories.action: Remove the Idunno.AntiCsrf library from all projects immediately.

stories.title: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
stories.abstract: Threat actors leveraged previously undisclosed vulnerabilities in Mitel MiCollab software to facilitate extortion attempts. Security researchers suggest that the attackers utilized artificial intelligence tools to accelerate the exploitation process, successfully compromising systems before the vendor issued official security guidance.
stories.why: The use of AI to weaponize zero-day vulnerabilities indicates a shift toward faster, more efficient exploitation cycles for enterprise communication platforms.
stories.action: Update Mitel MiCollab to the latest version immediately.

stories.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
stories.abstract: Broadcom released security updates for multiple VMware products, including ESX, vCenter, and Workstation. The most severe issue is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service, tracked as CVE-2026-123903, which carries a CVSS score of 9.8.
stories.why: Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this flaw to gain unauthorized access to critical infrastructure management components, potentially leading to full environment compromise.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for VMware vCenter and related products immediately.

stories.title: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers
stories.abstract: CISA has issued an advisory regarding a critical vulnerability affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA series controllers. These devices, widely deployed in commercial settings to regulate refrigeration, HVAC, and lighting, are susceptible to exploitation that could disrupt essential retail infrastructure operations.
stories.why: Compromised facility controllers can lead to physical damage, inventory loss, or unauthorized access to broader operational technology networks.
stories.action: Review the Danfoss advisory and apply recommended firmware updates to affected controllers immediately.

stories.title: Critical Cisco Expressway Flaw Exploited in Attacks
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-76466, affecting its Expressway Series and TelePresence Video Communication Server. The flaw carries a maximum CVSS severity rating of 9.8, indicating a high risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.why: The vulnerability is currently being leveraged by threat actors in the wild, posing an immediate risk to perimeter security infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Cisco for Expressway and TelePresence systems immediately.

stories.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
stories.abstract: Rackspace is shuttering its Spot cloud platform following a security compromise. The company is forcing users to migrate their workloads and rotate credentials immediately, citing the incident as the primary driver for the sudden service termination.
stories.why: Sudden service shutdowns following breaches often indicate deep-seated architectural failures or persistent unauthorized access that cannot be remediated in a timely manner.
stories.action: Migrate all workloads and rotate any credentials previously used within the Rackspace Spot environment.

stories.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
stories.abstract: The provided source material is too thin to confirm specific details regarding Amazon's claims about AI-driven zero-day exploitation. The excerpt mentions the Cairn AI framework but lacks sufficient context to explain the alleged incident or the mechanics of the reported attack.
stories.why: Automated exploitation of zero-days by AI agents represents a significant shift in threat actor capabilities and defensive response requirements.

stories.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack
stories.abstract: Peninsula Energy suspended operations at its Wyoming uranium facility following a cyberattack that compromised industrial control systems. The company has not provided a timeline for resuming production as it works to restore affected infrastructure.
stories.why: This incident highlights the ongoing vulnerability of critical infrastructure and operational technology environments to targeted cyber disruptions.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively chaining the Fragnesia vulnerability with PHP2Shell to compromise Palo Alto Networks firewalls. By targeting management interfaces exposed to the public internet, threat actors can gain root-level access to vulnerable appliances.
stories.why: Exploitation allows remote code execution and full system takeover, posing a critical risk to perimeter security infrastructure.
stories.action: Restrict management interface access to trusted networks and apply the latest vendor security patches immediately.

stories.title: [Control systems] Hitachi security advisory (AV26-1208)
stories.abstract: Hitachi Energy has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities affecting its RTU500 series CMU firmware across several versions, as well as the Cosminexus Component Container. These flaws could potentially impact the stability or security of industrial control system components.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial control systems like the RTU500 series present significant risks to critical infrastructure availability and operational integrity.
stories.action: Review Hitachi Energy security advisories and apply firmware updates for affected RTU500 and Cosminexus components.

stories.title: GitLab security advisory (AV26-1210)
stories.abstract: GitLab has released security updates for multiple versions of its Community and Enterprise editions to address newly identified vulnerabilities. Administrators should review the latest release notes and upgrade their instances to the specified patched versions to ensure system integrity.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in development infrastructure can lead to unauthorized access, code manipulation, or exposure of sensitive intellectual property.
stories.action: Update GitLab to the latest patched version corresponding to your current release branch.

stories.title: 13 Malicious NuGet Packages Turn Fake .NET Job Assessments Into Malware Delivery Traps
stories.abstract: Threat actors are distributing 13 malicious NuGet packages disguised as legitimate UI components for .NET developers. These packages, often masquerading as WinUI or WPF controls, are delivered through fraudulent job assessments to compromise developer workstations with malware.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting developers provide attackers with direct access to internal source code, build environments, and sensitive corporate credentials.
stories.action: Audit NuGet dependencies for unauthorized packages and restrict external package installation in development environments.

stories.title: Florida ransomware recovery CEO indicted for allegedly paying hacker ransoms
stories.abstract: A federal grand jury indicted the CEO of a ransomware recovery company. Prosecutors allege the executive deceived clients regarding his firm's capabilities and funneled payments directly to cybercriminals to resolve incidents.
stories.why: This highlights the risks of vetting third-party incident response firms and the potential legal liabilities associated with unauthorized ransom payments.

stories.title: UK Home Office waved through border system without a working fix for bad data
stories.abstract: The UK Information Commissioner's Office issued a formal reprimand to the Home Office following significant data integrity issues. These failures led to incorrect border records, causing distress and potential wrongful detention for travelers over a period exceeding one year.
stories.why: Systemic data inaccuracies in government databases can lead to severe civil liberty violations and indicate poor internal data governance and audit controls.

stories.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633
stories.abstract: A use-after-free vulnerability in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation allows for potential memory corruption. Attackers could exploit this flaw to trigger crashes or potentially execute arbitrary code by sending specifically crafted HTTP/2 requests to a vulnerable server.
stories.why: Memory corruption vulnerabilities in core web infrastructure pose significant risks for remote code execution and service disruption.
stories.action: Update NGINX to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers
stories.abstract: Federal prosecutors charged a former cybersecurity executive with wire fraud. The individual allegedly deceived ransomware victims by secretly paying attackers to decrypt data, then billing clients for significantly higher amounts and keeping the surplus as personal profit.
stories.why: This highlights a severe insider threat and ethical breach within the incident response industry, potentially compromising victim security and trust.

stories.title: Adobe security advisory (AV26-1205)
stories.abstract: Adobe has released security updates for Experience Manager (AEM) Cloud Service, AEM 6.5, and AEM 6.5 LTS. These patches address vulnerabilities affecting various service packs and cumulative hotfixes, requiring administrators to verify their current versions against the latest security bulletins.
stories.why: Unpatched AEM instances are frequent targets for remote code execution and unauthorized data access within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Review Adobe security bulletins and apply the latest AEM patches and cumulative hotfixes.

stories.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach
We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
stories.abstract: Recent high-profile outages across major organizations like Microsoft and the FAA were coincidental failures rather than coordinated cyberattacks. These incidents highlight the inherent fragility of aging, centralized, and poorly maintained digital infrastructure that underpins modern society.
stories.why: Systemic fragility and reliance on unmaintained legacy code create significant operational risks that mimic the impact of malicious cyber activity.

stories.title: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series
stories.abstract: The Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA series controllers contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in an unauthenticated CGI handler. Remote attackers can exploit this via malicious HTTP POST requests to trigger memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code with webserver-level privileges.
stories.why: This critical flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution on industrial controllers, posing a significant risk to commercial facility infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA series firmware to a version beyond 5.4.0.

stories.title: SYS010 malware abuses browser management to spy on Gmail, Outlook
stories.abstract: The SYS010 infostealer is leveraging malicious Meta advertisements to compromise browsers. By enrolling victims into unauthorized enterprise management profiles, the malware forces the installation of malicious extensions designed to exfiltrate sensitive communications from Gmail and Outlook accounts.
stories.why: This technique bypasses standard browser protections by abusing legitimate enterprise management features to maintain persistence and access user data.
stories.action: Audit browser management policies and remove unauthorized enterprise profiles or suspicious extensions.

stories.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
stories.abstract: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 programming software versions 6.80 and earlier contain a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability. Opening a maliciously crafted project file can trigger memory corruption, potentially allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code or crash the application.
stories.why: This flaw impacts critical infrastructure sectors and allows remote code execution via file-based exploitation, posing a significant risk to industrial control environments.
stories.action: Update C-More EA9 Programming Software to a version beyond 6.80.

stories.title: CTO of 'RansomwareHelp' Indicted for Wire Fraud
stories.abstract: The chief technology officer of RansomwareHelp has been indicted on federal wire fraud charges. The case highlights legal scrutiny surrounding firms that facilitate ransom negotiations and payments between victims and cybercriminal groups.
stories.why: It underscores the increasing legal risks for intermediaries operating in the ransomware ecosystem and potential regulatory shifts regarding ransom payments.

stories.title: Fake paid expert interviews impersonate brands to steal Google logins
stories.abstract: A phishing campaign named GoodGuys is targeting professionals with fraudulent invitations for paid expert consultations. Attackers impersonate well-known corporations to lure victims into providing their Google and Okta credentials via malicious landing pages.
stories.why: This social engineering tactic bypasses traditional technical filters by leveraging professional trust and high-value lures to harvest enterprise authentication tokens.
stories.action: Implement FIDO2-compliant hardware security keys for all Google and Okta authentication.

stories.title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
stories.abstract: Reports indicate that unidentified threat actors successfully compromised an open-source intelligence analysis platform utilized by the Central Intelligence Agency. Details regarding the scope of the intrusion, the specific data accessed, or the methods employed by the attackers remain currently undisclosed.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to intelligence infrastructure poses significant risks to national security, operational security, and the integrity of sensitive analytical data.

stories.title: Hackers Compromise 24 Check Point Management Servers in Suspected AI-Driven Attack Campaign
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting Check Point Security Management servers to compromise at least 22 global organizations. The campaign, identified as GT13, reportedly utilizes AI-assisted offensive tools to facilitate unauthorized access across sectors including government, energy, and finance.
stories.why: The use of AI-driven tooling suggests an evolving, automated threat landscape capable of scaling exploitation against critical infrastructure management interfaces.
stories.action: Audit Check Point Security Management server logs for unauthorized access and review security configurations.

stories.title: North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware
stories.abstract: A North Korean-linked threat actor dubbed PolinRider has compromised over 7,600 GitHub repositories. The campaign injects malicious Python loaders into utility files or conftest.py scripts, which execute upon import to facilitate further malware deployment.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting open-source repositories pose significant risks to downstream developers and automated CI/CD pipelines.
stories.action: Audit Python dependencies and review conftest.py files for unauthorized code injections.
